record.paper_title: Open problems on countable dense homogeneity
record.original_question: For n,m > 1 and uncountable cardinals kappa and lambda, determine the implications among higher-dimensional kappa-CDH and BA properties: does R^n being omega_1-CDH imply R^m is omega_1-CDH; does BA(R^n,kappa) imply BA(R^n,lambda) when kappa > lambda; does BA(R,omega_1) imply BA(R^n,omega_1) for all n > 1; and does BA(R^n,kappa) imply that R^n is kappa-CDH? Here kappa-CDH means that any two indexed families of pairwise disjoint countable dense sets can be matched coordinatewise by a self-homeomorphism, while BA(X,kappa) means any two kappa-dense subsets of X can be matched by a self-homeomorphism.

evidence.quote: Inspired by this fact, let us call a space X κ-CDH if given two families {Aα : α<κ} and {Bα : α<κ} of pairwise disjoint countable dense sets there is a homeomorphism h ∈ H (X) such that h[Aα] = Bα for every α<κ.

Problem 20 (Stepr¯ans–Watson). (1) Does Rn being ω1-CDH imply that Rm is ω1-CDH for n, m > 1? (2) Does BA(Rn, κ) imply BA(Rn, λ) when κ > λ? (3) Does BA(R, ω1) imply BA(Rn, ω1) for all n > 1? (4) Does BA(Rn, κ) imply that Rn is κ-CDH for n > 1 and κ uncountable?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{H}(X)$ denote the group of self-homeomorphisms of a topological space $X$. For an uncountable cardinal $\kappa$, say that $X$ is $\kappa$-CDH if for any two families $\{A_\alpha : \alpha < \kappa\}$ and $\{B_\alpha : \alpha < \kappa\}$ of pairwise disjoint countable dense subsets of $X$, there exists $h \in \mathcal{H}(X)$ such that $h[A_\alpha] = B_\alpha$ for every $\alpha < \kappa$. A subset $D \subseteq X$ is called $\kappa$-dense if $|D \cap U| = \kappa$ for every nonempty open set $U \subseteq X$. Write $\mathrm{BA}(X, \kappa)$ for the statement: for any two $\kappa$-dense subsets $D_1, D_2$ of $X$, there exists $h \in \mathcal{H}(X)$ with $h[D_1] = D_2$.

Determine the following implications, where $n, m > 1$ are integers and $\kappa, \lambda$ are uncountable cardinals:

(1) Does $\mathbb{R}^n$ being $\omega_1$-CDH imply that $\mathbb{R}^m$ is $\omega_1$-CDH?

(2) Does $\mathrm{BA}(\mathbb{R}^n, \kappa)$ imply $\mathrm{BA}(\mathbb{R}^n, \lambda)$ whenever $\kappa > \lambda$?

(3) Does $\mathrm{BA}(\mathbb{R}, \omega_1)$ imply $\mathrm{BA}(\mathbb{R}^n, \omega_1)$ for every $n > 1$?

(4) Does $\mathrm{BA}(\mathbb{R}^n, \kappa)$ imply that $\mathbb{R}^n$ is $\kappa$-CDH for every $n > 1$ and every uncountable $\kappa$?
artifact.status_search_result: A recent (2025) survey on countable dense homogeneity and topological groups still references these Steprāns–Watson questions in their original form, and no resolution of the four implications appears in the searchable literature. The problems concerning $\kappa$-CDH and $\mathrm{BA}(\mathbb{R}^n,\kappa)$ in higher dimensions appear to remain open.
